Metadata.Summary: Derm Foundation is a machine learning model that generates embeddings for dermatology images, enabling efficient AI model development for dermatology image analysis. It helps businesses and institutions leverage their dermatology data more effectively, needing less data and compute to build AI models [SOURCE 1].

UsesAndDirections.IntendedUseAndWorkflow: Derm Foundation is intended to reduce the training data, compute, and technical expertise necessary to develop task-specific models for skin image analysis. Embeddings can be used for classifying clinical conditions, scoring severity, identifying body parts, and determining image quality [SOURCE 4].

Warnings.ModelLimitations: The quality of Derm Foundation can degrade in extreme lighting conditions. The SFT model was trained on data from a limited set of countries and settings, so it may not generalize well to data from other countries, patient populations, or image types not used in training [SOURCE 4].

TrustIngredients.FoundationModelsUsedInApplicationIfAppli: Derm Foundation uses a BiT-M ResNet101x3 CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) architecture.
TrustIngredients.TrainingData: Derm Foundation was trained in two stages: pre-training using image-text pairs from the public web, and fine-tuning using tele-dermatology datasets from the United States and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images [SOURCE 4].
TrustIngredients.ValidationTestDataset: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across a range of skin-related classifications tasks. Training a linear classifier on Derm-Foundations embeddings were substantially more performant than doing the same for a standard BiT-M model [SOURCE 4].
TrustIngredients.SkinToneDiversity: The SFT model was trained on data from the United States, Colombia, Australia, and public images and may not generalize well to data from other countries or patient populations.
